answer: Force each identity to climb a public capability trellis: the network assigns a ladder of unpublished tasks of rising difficulty, and only peer-attested completions unlock the next rung. Reaching the zenith of settlement weight then costs real compute on every key, so a clone farm cannot mint influence for free. Keys that skip rungs, time out, or share near-identical traces are collapsed into one hollow cluster with a single seat, making mass signup cheaper to ignore than to run.
